name: Penken-Joch
kurzbeschreibung: The Penken-Joch is a popular viewpoint and starting point for stunning hikes in the Mayrhofen mountain region.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Penkenjoch (2,095 m) commands a sun-drenched alpine plateau high above the premier holiday destinations of Mayrhofen and Finkenberg in the central Zillertal valley. Globally acclaimed in winter as the buzzing epicenter of the "Ski Zillertal 3000" arena—featuring Austria's steepest groomed run, the infamous "Harakiri"—Penken transforms in summer into an exhilarating adventure mountain for families, hikers, and adrenaline seekers. The undisputed architectural crown of the plateau is the Granatkapelle (Garnet Chapel), conceived by world-renowned Swiss architect Mario Botta. Designed as a sharp rhombic dodecahedron clad in weathering Corten steel and local larch, it mirrors serenely across the turquoise waters of the Penken reservoir lake, paying homage to the valley's historic garnet mining heritage. From the plateau, 360-degree vistas sweep from the glaciated Olperer horn across the Tux and Zillertal Alps.

Route & Requirements

Thanks to state-of-the-art gondolas, the Penkenjoch caters seamlessly to all fitness levels. A beloved classic for families and casual walkers is the level circuit around the Penken reservoir to the Garnet Chapel: wide, well-maintained gravel lanes are stroller and wheelchair accessible, dotted with ergonomic timber loungers and water fun stations (45 to 60 minutes, easy grade T1). Mountain trekkers utilize the pass as a launching pad for ridge ascents to Mount Penken (2,227 m) or demanding crossings to the Rastkogel summit (2,762 m; 5 hours, alpine grade T3). Vertical adventurers flock to the limestone crags of Knorrennadel, featuring certified sport climbing crags and the scenic Knorren Via Ferrata (grade B/C, climbing harness and helmet required). The wide ridges also serve as one of Europe's premier launch points for tandem paragliders catching thermal updrafts over the valley. Sturdy sneakers suffice for the reservoir promenade, while ankle-high hiking boots are essential for mountain ascents. Leashed dogs are warmly welcomed on the plateau.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel aboard the historic Zillertalbahn to the Mayrhofen terminal station, enjoying a brief 5-minute stroll through town to the modern 3S Penkenbahn gondola terminal. Alternatively, regional valley buses connect to Finkenberg for the Finkenberger Almbahn gondola directly to Penkenjoch. Drivers take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal) and follow the B169 highway south into Mayrhofen, where multi-story garage parking is available at the lift base. Cable cars run daily from mid-May through late October between 8:30 AM and 5:00 PM.

Tips

Step inside Mario Botta's Granatkapelle: the ethereal interior lighting and extraordinary acoustic warmth create an unforgettable contemplative ambiance. Dine on the sun terrace of the adjacent Granatalm restaurant, savoring wood-fired pizzas and homemade Zillertaler Krapfen pastries while watching colorful paragliders take flight over the reservoir.
